The competition among MSM programs is intense, with a large number of institutions offering these degrees.
Programs strive to differentiate themselves by emphasizing unique curricular components such as leadership development modules, capstone projects, or global immersion experiences, which are designed to enhance employability and prepare graduates for management roles.
The rise of digital learning technologies has also led many institutions to offer MSM programs in online or hybrid formats, further increasing their reach and intensifying competition as geographic barriers to enrollment are reduced.
To stand out in a crowded market, programs often seek accreditation from prestigious bodies like AACSB, AMBA, or EQUIS and aim to secure favorable rankings from notable publications.
Many programs also forge partnerships with businesses and other organizations to help in curriculum development, provide real-world learning opportunities, and facilitate networking and job placements for graduates.

Recent trends in MSM programs include an increased emphasis on technology and analytics to integrate digital technologies in business, a focus on sustainability and social responsibility reflecting broader societal concerns, and more customizable and flexible learning paths to attract a diverse student body with varying needs and career goals.
Overall, the market for MSM programs remains robust, driven by their relevance, accessibility, and adaptability to market needs and educational technologies, though programs must continuously innovate and adapt to remain competitive.

OPEN FACULTY FORUM: Textbooks and other Course Materials’ availability from the University Bookstore and Library - Faculty Senate Vice President Williams provided some background information on the issue, noting that faculty have an ethical obligation as well as a legal one to use the university bookstore as a clearinghouse for course materials. Because buy-backs and rental options have all but disappeared, early adoption of textbooks is crucial if the bookstore is to be able to provide them in a timely fashion. The growth in use of apps and other alternatives poses special challenges for certain groups of students, especially international and talent development students and those relying on Federal Financial Aid. Useful suggestions pertained to providing information to students during orientation regarding course materials and involving department heads and deans in course material decisions to help ensure an equitable approach. A representative of the Campus Bookstore, Manager Paul Whitney, was on hand to offer their perspective. He noted that publishers’ “editioning” and the rise of Amazon are two of the biggest changes the industry has seen in the last couple of decades. Some faculty members complained that there seems to be excess bureaucracy involved in dealing with the campus bookstore in that, even if the course is not requiring materials through the bookstore, their forms still need to be completed every year. It was suggested that there may be a technical fix to help reduce that burden.

FACULTY SENATE OFFICE FACULTY SENATE LEGISLATION NOVEMBER 14, 2024 Graduate Council Report 2024-2025-02B At the November 4, 2024 meeting of the Graduate Council, the following matters were considered and are now presented to the Faculty Senate for approval. Curricular Matters Which Require Confirmation by The Faculty Senate PROGRAM MODIFICATIONS COLLEGE OF THE ENVIRONMENT & LIFE SCIENCES: PhD Marine Affairs, Effective Spring 2025 Appendix A The proposed changes include changing the credential type to “Degree”, initiation date of Spring 2025, change in location to “Kingston”, and changing required course credits to 21 from 18 plus an additional 45 credits instead of 48 credits. We are adding a new core course requirement of MAF 521 Coastal Zone Law. We have created a 500 level version of MAF 482, which is MAF 583 Quantitative Methods in Marine Affairs. The MAF 583 requirement replaces the MAF 482 requirement, since PhD students are not able to count 400 level courses toward their degree requirements. MA Marine Affairs, Effective Spring 2025 Appendix B We are adding a new core course requirement of MAF 521 Coastal Zone Law and reducing the total number of electives from 15 to 12. We are requiring that nine of the elective credits be within Marine Affairs. We have created a 500 level version of our MAF 482 course, which is MAF 583 Quantitative Methods in Marine Affairs. The MAF 583 requirement replaces the MAF 482 requirement. We have removed the option for MAF 598 Masters Project in order to streamline course codes.

Faculty determined that all MAF graduate students should take the Coastal Zone Law course in order to develop expertise in domestic coastal law as part of their degree program. The addition of this core course replaced one free elective, thus the total number of required credits (39) remains the same. MMA Marine Affairs, Effective Spring 2025 Appendix C We are adding a new core course requirement of MAF 521 Coastal Zone Law and reducing the total number of electives from 15 to 12. We are requiring that 50% of elective credits be within Marine Affairs. This change ensures that graduates of the Master of Marine Affairs program have expertise in domestic coastal law. Change in electives ensures that students take electives from within the department. Proposed changes include initiation date of Spring 2025, location change to “Kingston”; admission requirements to 3 instead of 5 years of post-graduate equivalent experience with the removal of “in marine areas employment”.
